questions.prompt: 1. Maya puts on her glasses before she reads a story. Which body part do the glasses help?
questions.evidence: Glasses help the eyes. Reading is something we do with our eyes, not with our ears or our hands.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Naming the body parts used for the five senses

questions.prompt: 2. Ali holds a bar of soap near his face. He says, “It is like flowers!” Which sense is he using?
questions.evidence: Noticing a scent with the nose is the sense of smell. Listening would need a sound, and touching would need his hand.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Choosing the sense verb that matches a situation

questions.prompt: 3. Grandma lifts a warm loaf from the oven and rests her hand on it. Choose True or False: she uses the sense of touch.
questions.evidence: Feeling how warm or soft something is uses the hand, so the sense is touch and the statement is true.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Linking an object to the sense used with it

questions.prompt: 4. Choose True or False: we hear with our eyes.
questions.evidence: We hear with our ears. Eyes are used for seeing.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Naming the body parts used for the five senses

questions.prompt: 5. Sami counts the chairs in the hall: ten, twenty, thirty … What is the next number word?
questions.evidence: The tens count goes ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty. After thirty comes forty.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading and writing the tens numbers

questions.prompt: 6. A sign in the library says there are 50 books on the new shelf. Which word means 50?
questions.evidence: Fifty is the number word for 50. Fifteen is 15 and five is 5.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading and writing the tens numbers

questions.prompt: 7. Continue this pattern: twenty, thirty, ______, fifty. Write the missing number word.
questions.evidence: The words go up by ten each time, so the word between thirty and fifty is forty.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Continuing a number pattern

questions.prompt: 8. Huda writes 33, 34, 35, 36 on the board. Which number should she write next?
questions.evidence: Counting on one from thirty-six gives thirty-seven; thirty-eight would skip a number.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Continuing a number pattern

questions.prompt: 9. Which numeral matches the number word forty-five?
questions.evidence: Forty-five is written as 45: four tens and five ones. 54 is fifty-four.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Matching a numeral to its word

questions.prompt: 10. A thick wall hides the kite from Rami. Complete his sentence: “I can’t ______ the kite.”
questions.evidence: A wall blocks what is in view, so the sense that fails is seeing.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using can and can’t about the senses

questions.prompt: 11. Nour wants to stroke a friendly kitten. Which question asks for permission?
questions.evidence: “Can I …?” asks the other person for permission. The other two are statements, not questions.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking for permission politely

questions.prompt: 12. Choose True or False: the polite answer to “Can I touch it?” is “Yes, you can.”
questions.evidence: “Yes, you can.” gives the permission that was asked for, and it changes I to you.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking for permission politely

questions.prompt: 13. Omar tastes his mother’s soup and wants to say it is very good to eat. Which word fits?
questions.evidence: Delicious describes food that tastes very good. Colourful is about colours and soft is about touch.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using describing words from the lesson

questions.prompt: 14. Sara holds a young kitten. It fits in one hand and feels gentle. Complete: “The kitten is ______ and soft.”
questions.evidence: A kitten that fits in one hand is small; small pairs naturally with soft.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using describing words from the lesson

questions.prompt: 15. Build the animal word from the lesson: g + oa + t. Write the whole word.
questions.evidence: Joining g, oa and t makes goat, one of the two printed oa words.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising and building the oa words

questions.prompt: 16. Write the word for the warm thing you wear outside: c + oa + t.
questions.evidence: Joining c, oa and t makes coat, the other printed oa word.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising and building the oa words

questions.prompt: 17. Which of these words contains the two letters oa?
questions.evidence: Goat is spelled g-o-a-t, so the letters oa are inside it. Gate and gift have no o.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising and building the oa words

questions.prompt: 18. Read Layla’s walk. Which sense does Layla use at the roses?
questions.evidence: The text says she enjoys their sweet smell, and it says she does not touch them.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading an unseen description of a senses walk

questions.prompt: 19. Read Layla’s walk again. Choose True or False: Layla touches the roses.
questions.evidence: The last sentence says she does not touch the roses because of the sharp thorns.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading an unseen description of a senses walk

questions.prompt: 20. Write a sentence beginning with I. Use all four words exactly once: can / smell / flowers / I.
questions.evidence: Beginning with I, the order is I + can + smell + flowers, which states an ability with the sense of smell.
questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing a clear English sentence
